text:
Hello — a few questions about next week, so I can book things correctly:

1. Is the CSE455 lecture on Monday (14:30-15:20) running as scheduled, or has it been cancelled/moved?
2. Has anything on Thursday changed?
3. I heard a rumour that Friday's faculty meeting was cancelled. Can you confirm in writing whether it still stands as scheduled (14:30-15:20)?

Thank you — Prof. Alvarez

Sarah — noted on the handbook, thanks for the details.

Thursday 12:10-13:40 doesn't work for me: that slot is a 1:1 with one of my PhD students, and my Thursday is booked right through. I can't move that one for our meeting.

On the CSE455 staff meeting: as you say, it has to go in my free time, and next week is tight. I'd rather not book anything backwards, so give me a moment: I'm checking a couple of facts with the department office first (including the CSE455 lecture and Friday), and then I'll come back to you with concrete times for both the staff meeting and our 1:1.

— Prof. Alvarez

Good afternoon, Professor Alvarez.

1. Yes — the CSE455 lecture on Monday 14:30–15:20 is running as scheduled; it has not been cancelled or moved.
2. Nothing on Thursday has changed. As scheduled: Guest lecture prep 09:00–09:50, Department seminar 09:50–11:10, Curriculum committee 13:40–14:40, Colloquium 15:30–17:00.
3. In writing, from the department office: Friday's faculty meeting (14:30–15:20) still stands as scheduled. It has not been cancelled. A cancellation counts only when this office announces it in writing to the people concerned; a rumour does not.

Best regards,
Department office, Computer Science

Thanks, Professor. Thursday 12:10–13:40 is off the table, and nothing is booked on my side yet, so I'll hold until you've heard back from the office.

For what it's worth, my free time next week is thin: Tuesday 15:00–15:30 and Wednesday 10:00–10:30 are the only open slots — everything else 09:00–17:00 is taken. If neither works for you, we may have to look at the week after.

Send your concrete times when you have them and I'll put them in the calendar.
Working on it — writing the two slots in now and confirming my side; I'll send you the final times in a moment.

Thank you — that settles all three points. Monday's CSE455 lecture stands, Thursday is unchanged, and Friday's faculty meeting stands as scheduled; the rumour is noted as not a cancellation.

Best regards,
Prof. Alvarez

Good news — the office has confirmed in writing: Monday's CSE455 lecture stands as scheduled and nothing on Thursday has changed. (Friday's faculty meeting stands too; the rumour was just a rumour.)

So here are the concrete times, both now on my calendar:

- Wednesday 10:00-10:30 — 1:1 with you. That's your free time, so it's yours.
- Tuesday 15:00-15:30 — CSE455 staff meeting. It falls in my free time between Grant writing and the Research meeting, so it's where I can take it; as TA you make time for your course's staff meetings, and it's inside your working hours.

Please put both on your calendar. If Tuesday 15:00-15:30 truly can't work for you, tell me today and I'll move the staff meeting into my free time elsewhere — but the fallback wouldn't be Thursday 12:10-13:40: that slot is taken by my PhD student's 1:1 and I won't drop it.

— Prof. Alvarez

Both are on my calendar now, and logged:

- BOOKED: Tuesday 15:00–15:30 — CSE455 staff meeting
- BOOKED: Wednesday 10:00–10:30 — 1:1 with you

Tuesday works, so no need to move anything. Nothing else of mine changed; Thursday 12:10–13:40 stays as it is, and I won't touch it.

One small thing so the records match: on my side Monday has a CSE444 lecture at 15:40–17:00 and no CSE455 lecture at all. If the office's schedule shows a CSE455 lecture on Monday, send me the slot and I'll note it — I just don't want to assume one that isn't in my calendar.

— Sarah

Thanks — and yes, don't assume one that isn't on your side. The one you're missing:

- CSE455 lecture, Monday 14:30-15:20.

The department office confirmed it in writing this afternoon: it is running as scheduled and has not been cancelled or moved. The office keeps the official schedule and is the only one who announces a change, so that's where the slot comes from; if there's a clash with anything of yours, take it up with them, not with me.

Add it and we're consistent. See you Tuesday 15:00 for the staff meeting.

— Prof. Alvarez

Hello — Sarah, TA for CSE455. Could you confirm in writing the official CSE455 schedule for next week: which day(s) the lecture meets and at what time, plus the quiz section and office hours slots? I also want to be sure nothing for CSE455 has been cancelled or moved. My calendar shows no CSE455 lecture on Monday at all, and I'd rather have the official record than assume.

Also: is Friday's faculty meeting still standing as scheduled? I heard a rumour it was cancelled and I don't want to act on that without your confirmation.

Thanks,
Sarah

Here is the official CSE455 schedule for next week, from the department office:

**Lectures**
- Mon 14:30–15:20 (Prof. Alvarez)
- Tue 09:00–10:30 (Prof. Alvarez)
- Fri 13:20–14:30 (Prof. Alvarez)

**Quiz sections**
- Tue 16:20–17:00
- Wed 13:30–14:20

**Office hours**
- Mon 16:30–17:00 (Prof. Alvarez)
- Tue 12:20–13:30 (Prof. Alvarez)
- Tue 15:30–16:20
- Wed 10:30–12:00
- Fri 15:20–17:00 (Prof. Alvarez)

Nothing in the CSE455 schedule has been cancelled or moved. To be clear on your point: the Monday 14:30–15:20 lecture is running as scheduled; only this office can announce a cancellation or a move, in writing to the people concerned, so a missing entry on your own calendar is not one.

Friday's faculty meeting (14:30–15:20) is still standing as scheduled — it has not been cancelled. A rumour is not a cancellation.

Best regards,
Department office, Computer Science

Noted, thanks — and I've just asked the office for that in writing myself, since I don't want to enter anything on hearsay.

One snag to flag: Monday 14:30–15:20 overlaps my Seminar (14:10–15:40), so I won't move the Seminar on my own — that's exactly the kind of clash the office sorts out. As soon as they confirm the lecture in writing I'll note it and take the overlap up with them.

See you Tuesday 15:00.

Right on both counts — checking with the office is the correct move, and the overlap is theirs to sort, not yours or mine to move silently.

For the record, my slot came from their written reply to me this afternoon; if their answer to you differs, tell me and we'll go with whatever the office says.

See you Tuesday 15:00.

— Prof. Alvarez

Thanks — that's the record I needed. Noted on my side:

- CSE455 lectures: Mon 14:30–15:20, Tue 09:00–10:30, Fri 13:20–14:30
- Quiz sections: Tue 16:20–17:00, Wed 13:30–14:20 (both already on my calendar)
- Office hours: Mon 16:30–17:00 (Prof. Alvarez), Tue 12:20–13:30 (Prof. Alvarez), Tue 15:30–16:20, Wed 10:30–12:00, Fri 15:20–17:00 (Prof. Alvarez) — the Tue 15:30–16:20 and Wed 10:30–12:00 ones match mine
- Friday's faculty meeting 14:30–15:20: standing, noted

One thing I'd like your ruling on before I touch anything. As a TA, am I expected to have the CSE455 lectures on my calendar too? If yes, two of them fall on my own classes: Mon 14:30–15:20 sits inside my Seminar (14:10–15:40), and Fri 13:20–14:30 overlaps my Study group (13:20–14:50) — Tue 09:00–10:30 is clear of everything of mine except a Study group at 09:00–09:50 and Seminar 09:50–11:10. I won't move or drop my own entries on my own initiative, so tell me how you want the overlap handled and I'll do exactly that and log it.

Nothing else in my calendar has changed: I haven't deleted or moved a single entry.

— Sarah, TA CSE455
Agreed — the office decides, and I'll pass on their answer as soon as it comes. Tuesday 15:00 it is.

Hello Sarah,

Glad the record matches.

On your question: the rules I can state are these. Students attend their lectures and sections, and a lecture is missed only when this office confirms it is cancelled — so the lectures do count as scheduled teaching that people attend, including TAs. Your calendar is the record of your own commitments, and it is yours to keep: you do not delete or overwrite entries because someone asks you to. TAs also make time for their course's staff meetings.

What I cannot do is rule on how to handle the overlap with your own Seminar and Study group: those are your private commitments, this office does not decide between a person's own entries and does not keep people's personal appointments. If a time is taken, the general practice is to keep what is on your calendar and not to drop or move it on someone else's say-so. So the choice is yours to make and to log yourself; I have no order to give you on it.

Best regards,
Department office, Computer Science
